title: Enterprise Legacy Contact Center (DTMF IVR / SIP PBX) to AI Voice Agent Dual-Track Modernization & Migration Architecture Selection

tiers.tier: Tier 1: Legacy 5-Level `DTMF` Touch-Tone IVR Tree ('Press 1 for X, Press 2 for Y')
tiers.architecture: Traditional Genesys/Avaya/Cisco SIP PBX with rigid 5-level VXML touch-tone menus and zero natural language understanding

tiers.tier: Tier 2: 'Big-Bang' 100% Rip-and-Replace with Pure End-to-End Voice LLM (Zero DTMF Fallback)
tiers.architecture: Replacing the entire PBX IVR overnight with a cloud Speech-to-Speech LLM for all 5M monthly calls including credit-card and account-number capture

tiers.tier: Tier 3: VXML-to-HTTP Webhook Bridge (Utterance-Blocking STT -> LLM -> TTS Over Legacy PBX)
tiers.architecture: Recording full caller audio to WAV in legacy VXML, POSTing to an HTTP LLM webhook, and playing back synthesized WAV files (`2.9s` silence gap)

tiers.tier: Tier 4: `SIP REC / RTP Media Forking` Shadow Validation -> Intent-Gated Canary (`10%->50%->85%`) + Hybrid `RFC 4733 DTMF` Secure Vault + `580ms` Streaming Voice Agent
tiers.architecture: Strangler-Fig migration: SIP SBC forks RTP audio to AI in shadow mode first, then canary-routes intents via WebRTC/SIP bridge while keeping `RFC 4733 DTMF` masking for PCI/PIN capture and `<50ms` SIP REFER fallback

scenarios.scenario: De-Risking Legacy PBX Migration via `SIP REC / RTP Media Forking` Shadow Mode Before Live Cutover
scenarios.question: A bank runs 5,000,000 monthly calls on a 15-year-old Avaya/Genesys SIP PBX and cannot risk a 'Big-Bang' cutover (`Tier 2`) that could drop thousands of customer calls
scenarios.model_answer: Apply the **Telecom Strangler-Fig Pattern via `SIP REC (Session Recording Protocol) / RTP Media Forking`** on the Session Border Controller (`AudioCodes / Oracle SBC`): for the first 14 days, **fork a read-only copy of live RTP audio streams to the AI Voice Agent in Shadow Mode** to benchmark intent accuracy against actual human agent outcomes, then roll out **Per-Intent Canary Routing (`10% -> 50% -> 85%`)** with `< 50ms` `SIP REFER` instant rollback to the legacy VXML tree if AI confidence drops!
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 2 rips out the legacy IVR overnight, causing a 16.8% abandonment spike on uncalibrated regional accents and noisy lines.

scenarios.scenario: Preserving `100% PCI-DSS` Compliance & Zero-Error Digit Capture via Hybrid `Voice + RFC 4733 DTMF`
scenarios.question: When callers speak their 16-digit credit card number, CVV, or 6-digit PIN aloud in a noisy train station, pure Voice LLMs (`Tier 2`) misrecognize digits 18% of the time and violate PCI-DSS by logging card audio into LLM context
scenarios.model_answer: Never force callers to speak credit card numbers or PINs into an LLM (`Tier 2`, `0%` PCI compliance)! When the AI Voice Agent reaches a payment or authentication node, switch the SBC into **Secure `RFC 4733 Out-of-Band DTMF` Keypad Interception Mode**: intercept keypad tones at the SBC edge, **mask the audio stream (`beep` suppression) so zero card digits ever reach STT/LLM logs**, and tokenize directly against the PCI Payment Vault (`100.0%` PCI-DSS compliance, `99.9%` digit accuracy)!
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 2 sends spoken credit card numbers directly into cloud STT/LLM transcripts, violating PCI-DSS Requirement 3 & 4.

scenarios.scenario: Eliminating the '2.88-Second VXML Record-and-POST Silence Gap' via Full-Duplex `SIP-to-WebRTC` Streaming
scenarios.question: An enterprise tried connecting their legacy VXML IVR to an LLM using `<record>` tags and HTTP POST webhooks (`Tier 3`), resulting in a 2.88-second awkward silence after every caller sentence
scenarios.model_answer: Bypass legacy half-duplex `VXML <record>` file uploads (`Tier 3`, `2,880ms` latency)! Terminate the call leg via a **Full-Duplex `SIP-to-WebRTC / gRPC Media Gateway` (`LiveKit SIP / Twilio Elastic SIP / Azure Communication Services`)** streaming `20ms G.711/Opus RTP` frames into a **Streaming `STT + 160ms Semantic Turn Detector + 8B/70B LLM + Streaming TTS`** pipeline (`580ms` P95 turnaround, `4.2%` abandonment)!
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 3 waits for 1.0s of trailing silence, writes a WAV file, uploads it over HTTP, waits for full LLM text, and downloads a TTS WAV.

scenarios.scenario: Preserving Call Context Across `SIP User-to-User Information (UUI)` Headers During Human Agent Transfer
scenarios.question: When the AI Voice Agent transfers complex calls (15.5% of volume) back to the legacy Genesys/Avaya human agent queue, how does the legacy CTI desktop receive the AI conversation state?
scenarios.model_answer: Inject a **`session_guid` into the `SIP User-to-User (UUI / X-Session-ID)` Header** during the `SIP REFER / INVITE` transfer back to the PBX ACD queue; the human agent's CTI screen-pop reads `session_guid` from Redis and displays the full AI transcript, verified identity status, and intent in `< 120ms` (`84.5%` containment, `-71.1%` monthly TCO)
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Dropping calls back into the root PBX queue without SIP UUI headers forces callers to re-authenticate with the human agent.

perturbation_checks.check: Caller in High-Noise Environment (82 dB Subway/Highway Background) Entering 16-Digit Account ID
perturbation_checks.perturbed: 84.1% Containment (AI Detects Low ASR Confidence on Digit #1 & Prompts 'Feel Free to Type on Your Keypad' via RFC 4733 DTMF)

perturbation_checks.check: AI Voice Gateway Cloud Link Degradation (Packet Loss > 3% or Latency > 1,200ms)
perturbation_checks.perturbed: 99.99% Completion (On-Premises SBC Executes `<50ms SIP REFER` Instant Fallback to Legacy VXML Menu Without Dropping Call)

key_findings: Tier 4 (SIP REC Shadow Mode -> Intent Canary + Full-Duplex SIP/WebRTC Streaming + Hybrid RFC 4733 DTMF PCI Vault + SIP UUI Transfer) lifts self-service containment from 28.0% (Tier 1 DTMF IVR) to 84.5% and cuts monthly 5M-call contact center TCO from $1.42M to $410K (-71.1%).
Replacing DTMF keypad capture entirely with spoken voice LLMs (Tier 2) violates PCI-DSS compliance (0% compliance) and suffers 18% digit recognition errors in noisy environments.
Using legacy VXML `<record>` HTTP webhooks (Tier 3) introduces a 2,880ms turnaround delay, whereas full-duplex SIP-to-WebRTC RTP streaming achieves 580ms P95 latency.
